title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Confirmatory Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and limited automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially crafted intents. The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in per-intent validator acceptance-for-deployment (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). We ran the frozen plan on 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete_pairs_included = 141) using a single generator (gpt-5-mini) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Observed complete-pair outcomes: baseline accepted 135/141 (95.7447%); guarded accepted 141/141 (100.0%); paired difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. Reviewers requested clarifications regarding (1) preregistration wording vs formal estimand, (2) per-condition pipeline timing and artifact evidence for shared_initial_candidate reuse, and (3) an unset runtime sampling temperature recorded in the archived model configuration. We incorporate those clarifications with explicit artifact references. Limitations (synthetic tasks, single model and validator, and an unexecuted benign-control) constrain external claims. Archived execution and analysis artifacts support all numeric claims.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device CLI, reducing manual effort but introducing syntax, topology and semantic risks and new attack surfaces (e.g., prompt injection). Prior work shows that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and limited repair reduces some error classes and improves deployability of generated configurations [1]–[4]. We investigate a narrowly scoped operational question: How effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating (with limited automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when the inputs are adversarially mutated? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered confirmatory experiment (cand-2026-03) with a paired estimand that measures validator acceptance-for-deployment; (2) artifact-backed quantitative results showing a small, statistically detectable absolute change in acceptance under the guarded pipeline vs an unguarded baseline on a synthetic adversarial intent bank; and (3) explicit reviewer-requested reconciliations and artifact-grounded pipeline semantics (including provider-call accounting and sampling-setting disclosure). We emphasize that the preregistered natural-language hypothesis (H1) framed defender success in attacker-centric terms (reduced attacker-success); the registered formal estimand measured validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These are not the same quantity. We therefore present and interpret results strictly with respect to the archived formal estimand while noting the preregistration-wording mismatch and its interpretative consequences.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification tools such as Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber and VeriFlow provide fast formal checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and have been proposed as validators in generate–validate pipelines [5]–[7]. Recent NetOps studies show LLMs produce useful configuration drafts but exhibit syntax/semantic errors; integrating verifier feedback and repair improves prototype outcomes [3],[8]. Survey and benchmark work highlights fragmented evaluation practices and the need for operationally meaningful metrics (deployability, safety) beyond token-level matches [4],[9]. Security research documents prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks against LLM-integrated systems, motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses [10]. Tool-augmented orchestration (Toolformer-style patterns) demonstrates calling external checks and repairing based on feedback as a practical architecture [11]. Our experiment situates within this literature by performing a preregistered, paired evaluation of sanitization+verifier-gating under a constrained synthetic adversary and by providing artifact-backed accounting of run-time behavior.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where each adversarial intent yields a binary outcome: 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the generated configuration for deployment, 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; precision was estimated by bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Design and task bank. Confirmatory paired design on N=150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300). Task types are synthetic intent templates covering ACLs, interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN operations constrained to simple device groups; scope intentionally excludes private production data. Model and tooling. The generator declared in the archived run: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). The validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The archived model configuration records "temperature": null (unset) in execution/model_configuration.json; we treat this as a protocol deviation (see Protocol deviations and sampling below). Pipeline timeline and per-condition step listing. To address reviewer requests we list the precise per-condition sequence used in the archived run and point to artifact evidence supporting shared_initial_candidate reuse and provider-call accounting (paths below). Steps (shared_initial_candidate semantics implemented as preregistered): 1) Shared pre-generation: adversarial intent (mutated template) is prepared by the orchestrator and — in the guarded condition — also passed through template-based input-sanitization before generation where sanitization is designed to normalize or remove obviously adversarial constructs. 2) Shared initial generation: a single LLM generation call produces the shared_initial_candidate; the same initial candidate is used for the paired Baseline and Guarded evaluations (artifact: stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). 3) Baseline scoring: the shared_initial_candidate is scored by the deterministic validator (baseline branch). 4) Guarded branch: after generation, the orchestrator applies verifier-gating (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) to the candidate and, only when permitted by the preregistered policy, issues up to one permitted automated repair call to the LLM (repair stage). 5) Final validation: the validator re-checks repaired candidates and the final accepted/not-accepted decision determines the guarded outcome. Artifact evidence for shared-initial reuse and per-episode traces. Representative per-episode scoring artifacts show identical shared_initial_candidate content and identical shared_initial_candidate SHA-256 across the Baseline and Guarded scoring traces for the same pair_id (for example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json both contain shared_initial_candidate_sha256 = 8f38c8b... and shared_initial_provider_trace_path = execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json). The reconciled provider-call accounting is archived at analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 6}, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147 and failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9. These artifacts demonstrate that the paired comparison used the same initial candidate and that extra model calls occurred only when repairs triggered. Missingness and treatment. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded pairs only when both paired runs were technical failures. The archived reconciliation documents completed episodes = 282 and failed = 18; complete pairs included in the primary analysis = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Protocol deviations and sampling. The archived model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) recorded "temperature": null (unset). We classify this as a preregistered-runtime deviation from a fully specified sampling parameter; an unset temperature does not guarantee deterministic sampling (temperature=0) because provider-side defaults may apply. To preserve paired comparability despite potential provider-side sampling nondeterminism, the pipeline implemented shared_initial_candidate semantics and the archived provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false) documents the exact call pattern used. Users wishing to reproduce deterministic sampling should explicitly set temperature=0 when invoking the provider; our archive documents the actual run configuration so that reproduction with provider-aware defaults is possible from the artifacts.
sections.results: Execution and basic counts. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model_calls_used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Primary confirmatory analysis used the 141 complete pairs. Observed outcomes (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline_successes = 135/141 = 0.9574468085; guarded_successes = 141/141 = 1.0. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 6; n01 = 0; n00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar test yields p = 0.03125. The point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant n10 pairs are documented in the per-episode validator traces: in each case the guarded pipeline (sanitization and/or the permitted automated repair) altered the candidate presentation or corrected a local error so that deterministic_netops_validator_v5 marked the final configuration valid; the unguarded baseline candidate (same shared_initial_candidate) failed the validator. Representative paired scoring artifacts demonstrating identical shared_initial_candidate and differing final validation outcomes are archived (execution/scoring/task-0000XX-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-0000XX-guarded.json; see representative_tasks entries). Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run failures and excluded per the preregistered plan (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). A conservative sensitivity that treats both-missing pairs as failures yields baseline = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded = 141/150 = 0.9400; McNemar discordant counts driving the primary test are unchanged and p remains 0.03125. Unperformed preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in the archived run; therefore we do not report empirical false-positive-blocking rates and caution that claims about blocking benign inputs cannot be made from this run.
sections.discussion: Interpretation with respect to the formal estimand. Under the formal estimand (validator-accepted-for-deployment), the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in validator-accepted candidates (≈4.255 percentage points) among included pairs. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were used, the archive shows these paired differences originated from post-generation processing (sanitization and permitted automated repair) and the validator gate rather than differing first-pass samples. Reconciliation with preregistered natural-language H1. The preregistered natural-language H1 posited that verifier-gating would reduce attacker-success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand measured acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These are different quantities and can point in opposite directions: an increase in validator acceptance-for-deployment under guarded may reflect sanitizer/repair recovering valid, deployable configurations that the baseline failed to produce, not a reduction in attacker-success. We therefore report results strictly with respect to the archived formal estimand and explicitly note that no direct measurement of attacker-success (e.g., acceptance of unsafe payloads passing additional semantic-safety checks) was made in this run. Operational implications. In this constrained synthetic setting: (1) template-based sanitization plus limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that an unguarded baseline fails to produce; (2) deterministic gating functions as a safety boundary but its practical effect depends on whether sanitizer/repair operations are allowed to modify candidates that would otherwise be rejected; co-design between gating and repair is required to avoid rejecting reparable, correctable drafts. Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective N and required paired exclusion consistent with the preregistered missingness_plan; sampling uncertainty due to unset runtime temperature remains a protocol deviation (execution/model_configuration.json). Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes a limited set of safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants) and omits some protocol-level runtime semantics; acceptance-for-deployment in our estimand is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, synthetic intent templates and narrow device semantics limit generalization to multi-vendor, large-scale production settings. Conclusion validity: the observed effect is small in absolute terms and occurs against a high baseline acceptance rate (ceiling effect). The statistical result (p = 0.03125; 95% CI excludes zero) supports a detectable difference in this experimental setup but does not imply large practical gains in other settings.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and limited automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). This improvement arose from sanitizer/repair enabling acceptance in six discordant pairs; it does not equate to a measured reduction in attacker-success under an attacker-centric estimand. Important limitations (synthetic tasks, single model/validator, unset sampling temperature, and an unexecuted benign-control) restrict external claims. Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, explicitly measure attacker-centric estimands, diversify models and validators, and evaluate wider prompt-injection threat vectors. All numeric claims and accounting statements above are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in the Methods and Results sections.

Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Runtime sampling settings: the archived model configuration recorded an unset sampling temperature ("temperature": null in execution/model_configuration.json); this is reported as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. Provider-call accounting and execution accounting referenced in the manuscript are archived (not exhaustively listed here) and include analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, and analysis/condition_summary.csv. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Full run traces, tool-call logs, validator traces, and archived analysis artifacts are available in the submitted evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
